items.title: Google AI Mode Cites Itself More Often, With More Organic Links
items.summary: Google's AI Mode self-citations have tripled from 5% to 17% over nine months, with 59% now pointing to organic search results rather than Google Business Profiles, indicating a shift beyond local search relevance. This change positions Google as the top-cited domain in 19 of 20 niches analyzed, emphasizing the continued importance of organic rankings in AI-driven visibility. For SEO, focus on optimizing for organic performance as AI Mode matures, per the February 2024 SE Ranking data.

items.title: How structured data supports local visibility across Google and AI
items.summary: Structured data (schema) now serves as a critical trust signal in AI-driven search environments, enabling Google and other AI systems to verify business information, reduce conflicts across local packs, AI Overviews, and search results, and reinforce entity consistency for improved local visibility. Key impacts include increased confidence in accurate, aligned signals like on-page content, Google Business Profiles, and reviews, while contradictions or false positives (e.g., mismatched hours or unauthorized reviews) lead to ignored markup and reduced visibility. Advice emphasizes using specific schema types like LegalService, Organization, Person, OfferCatalog, and FAQPage for local businesses, maintaining them through quarterly audits and trigger-based updates to reflect changes, ensuring reliability across fragmented search interfaces.

items.title: How to use AI for SEO without losing your brand voice
items.summary: AI excels at scaling SEO tasks like data analysis, keyword clustering, content outlining, and pattern detection, allowing teams to focus on strategy while reducing manual effort. However, without a defined brand voice, AI-generated content risks becoming generic and soulless, leading to diluted identity rather than penalties from Google, which penalizes low-quality content regardless of origin. To mitigate this, define brand voice clearly before using AI, train tools on existing content, use AI for structure and research while humans handle tone, storytelling, and editing, and prioritize human oversight on core pages for authenticity and trust-building.

items.title: How to revise your old content for AI search optimization
items.summary: AI search optimization (AEO) rewards revising old content by reformatting it for topical breadth and depth using a hub-and-spoke model, chunk-level retrieval with self-contained passages, and answer synthesis through clear summaries and non-promotional tones, enabling better visibility in AI answers. Prioritize content with expertise, proprietary insights, or frequent questions, focusing on reports, tools, and evergreen guides that tie to business growth, while updating metadata like title tags, headings, and meta descriptions to serve as context anchors rather than ranking levers.

items.title: Literature is 'in peril' due to 'social censure', Adichie claims in BBC Reith lecture
items.summary: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie claimed in her BBC Reith Lecture that literature is endangered by social censure and excessive caution in publishing. She criticized the widespread use of sensitivity readers by publishers and disclosed that one of her novels may soon face bans in certain American schools. Adichie urged for more courageous narrative approaches amid rising cultural sensitivities.

items.title: Media Do International to Acquire Seven Seas Entertainment
items.summary: Media Do International announced its acquisition of Seven Seas Entertainment, a prominent publisher of manga, light novels, danmei, and international storytelling. The deal highlights surging global demand for these genres across print, digital, and audio formats. Seven Seas will continue its publishing operations following the acquisition.

items.title: HarperCollins Ireland seizes Barry's 'stunning' coming-of-age story of Ireland 3.0
items.summary: HarperCollins Ireland acquired world rights to journalist Aoife Barry's debut novel Social Capital. The book is described as a coming-of-age tale capturing modern Ireland's evolution. Publication details will be announced soon.

items.title: BookTok is already spiraling for ACOTAR 6 and 7
items.summary: Sarah J. Maas announced two new books, ACOTAR 6 and 7, in her A Court of Thorns and Roses series on the Call Her Daddy podcast. BookTok erupted with excitement, driving viral discussions and speculation among fans. The reveals have intensified anticipation for future fantasy releases.

items.title: Rights Report: Week of March 2, 2026
items.summary: Publishers Weekly reported multiple significant rights deals, including world rights for a new children's book acquired by Lerner/Carolrhoda for summer 2027 publication. Deals negotiated by agents like Laura Rennert highlight ongoing activity across genres. The roundup showcases key acquisitions from the past week.

items.title: ‘A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms’ Star Reacts to Fan ‘Negativity’ About Her Race
items.summary: Tanzyn Crawford, star of 'A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms,' addressed fan negativity regarding her race in portraying Tanselle Too-Tall, stating she faced such criticism but remains employed and focused on her dreams. She received reassurance from George R.R. Martin, who confirmed she matched his vision for the character. The series, a 'Game of Thrones' prequel, saw strong viewership with 9.5 million U.S. viewers in its first three days.

items.title: Cardi B Allegedly Went Berserk at 'SNL' Rehearsal Over 'Weekend Update' Nicki Minaj Joke
items.summary: Cardi B allegedly became upset during rehearsal for 'SNL's 1,000th episode on January 31 and destroyed equipment after overhearing a 'Weekend Update' joke about Nicki Minaj's recent affiliation with MAGA. The incident occurred because of Cardi's longstanding beef with Nicki and a prior social media feud where Nicki targeted Cardi's children, despite the joke not being about Cardi. Sources report Cardi threatened to leave, threw her phone at a TV monitor, punched a screen in the producers' office until it broke, and the joke was ultimately scrapped.

items.title: Why Gen Z wants to buy and rent DVDs and Blu-rays in the age of streaming
items.summary: Gen Z is increasingly embracing DVDs and Blu-rays due to frustrations with streaming services, including subscription fatigue and scattered content availability, viewing physical media as a form of nostalgia and cultural rebellion. Video rental stores like Vidiots, Vidéothèque, and Cinefile report record rentals, purchases, and membership growth, with Vidiots doubling disc loans from 22,000 to 50,000 in a year and seeing over 1,000 weekly rentals in 2025. Physical media sales declined only 9% in 2025, down from over 20% drops in 2023 and 2024, while boutique companies like Criterion Collection experience significant year-over-year sales increases driven by young customers.

items.title: Watch TWICE Revisit Vibrant Hit 'Strategy' on 'Fallon'
items.summary: TWICE performed their song “Strategy,” featuring Megan Thee Stallion, on The Tonight Show to celebrate its inclusion in the Netflix animated film KPop Demon Hunters, which is nominated for Best Animated Feature at the Oscars. The track was originally released in 2024 as part of the group’s EP of the same name. Group members Jihyo, Chaeyoung, and Jeongyeon also recorded a new song “Takedown” for the film’s soundtrack.

items.title: Death in Paradise icon slams ‘woke’ trigger warnings as he shares hard times for industry
items.summary: Gary Wilmot, a recent addition to the cast of BBC's Death in Paradise, has criticised the increasing use of 'woke' trigger warnings on older TV programmes, stating there may be some harm in it going too far while acknowledging the need for guidance. He discussed the TV industry's challenges, including declining viewership for the BBC compared to platforms like YouTube, and described changes as evolution that makes him feel uncomfortable but not bitter. Wilmot, an advocate for theatre, is currently working on his stage play While They Were Waiting at London's Gatehouse Theatre.

items.title: ‘First Time Caller’ Movie in the Works From ‘Tell Me Lies’ Producer, A Cup of Happy Productions (EXCLUSIVE)
items.summary: A movie adaptation based on B.K. Borison’s 2025 romance novel “First Time Caller,” which follows a hopeless romantic meeting a jaded radio host in a “Sleepless in Seattle”–inspired love story, is in development. The film rights have been optioned by Daryl Steiger’s A Cup of Happy Productions, with Laura Lewis set to produce through Rebelle Media and Amy Huckabay writing the screenplay. Borison is attached as an executive producer for the project, the first installment in her planned “Heartstrings” trilogy.

items.title: No AI Plan, No Loan. Small Business Lenders Force Main Street To Face The Future
items.summary: Small business lenders are increasingly requiring applicants to demonstrate an understanding of AI's disruptive impact on their operations, as AI tools can perform tasks in industries like professional services and real estate more efficiently. Failure to address AI in loan applications can raise concerns about a business's oversight or competitiveness, potentially affecting loan approvals. Handled properly, showing adaptation to AI can strengthen applications by addressing future risks and efficiency gains.

items.title: Origami launches chat-based AI tool for sales leads
items.summary: Origami, a San Francisco-based startup, has launched a conversational AI prospecting product that generates sales lead lists from plain-English prompts and sells access via a flat monthly subscription. The tool offers a chat-style interface where users type requests for specific company and contact profiles and receive a ready-to-work lead list delivered within minutes. It provides better results for small and medium-sized companies and niche verticals with limited digital footprints.

items.title: wearemighty Launches SecretSauce, the AI Platform Delivering Always On-Brand Content at Scale
items.summary: wearemighty announced the launch of SecretSauce, an AI platform that memorizes brand identity once and applies it automatically to all content productions, turning AI-generated outputs into cohesive, on-brand assets. Designed for solopreneurs, creators, lean teams, and growing SMEs, it enables fast creation of social media content, product packaging, advertising, and more. It scales production efficiently, reducing agency timelines from hours to minutes and costs significantly while maintaining quality.

items.title: Smarsh unveils AI tool to cut compliance alert noise
items.summary: Smarsh has launched the Noise Reduction Agent, an AI-based tool within Smarsh Professional Archive that filters out low-risk digital communications before they enter compliance review queues, achieving over 60% reduction in false positives. It targets smaller financial firms and mid-sized businesses lacking staff for monitoring high volumes of alerts. The tool applies AI at ingestion to suppress noise affordably, reducing alert fatigue and backlogs for SMBs.

items.title: MYOB unleashes new AI tools for SME cashflow
items.summary: MYOB has introduced a suite of AI tools for SMEs in New Zealand and Australia, focusing on cashflow management, including smart invoice reminders that analyze late payer behavior and smart reconciliation using machine learning to auto-match transactions. AI business insights provide interactive charts and explanations to identify trends and performance drivers. The tools save time on repetitive tasks and address late payment issues without disrupting workflows.
